answer.message:
Suggested two-week plan: keep your existing group texts and current hours records—no new software needed.

Assign roles today
• You, the owner: set the rules and resolve exceptions neither manager can settle.
• Manager 1, Swap Lead: approve swaps across all three cafés, checking coverage and role suitability.
• Manager 2, Hours Lead: own Friday hours approval.
• Each manager is the other’s backup. Tell all 42 staff who is covering whenever either manager is absent. If both are unavailable, you make the decision.

Week 1: establish one clear process
1. Pin one swap template in each café’s existing group text: “Café | shift date/time | original worker | proposed replacement.” The replacement must explicitly accept; the Swap Lead then replies “APPROVED” or “NOT APPROVED.” Until approval, the original worker remains assigned. For an illness or emergency, staff should contact the duty manager directly rather than wait for a swap.
2. The approving manager updates your existing schedule immediately. Group texts are for requests; the schedule is the final reference.
3. By Thursday close, staff report missing or incorrect hours privately through your existing channel—not the group text. Managers review their assigned cafés before Friday’s approval; divide the three cafés explicitly today.
4. Set a Friday approval cutoff that leaves time before your payroll deadline. If the Hours Lead is absent, the Swap Lead takes over using the same records and unresolved-issues list. Escalate disputed hours to you; don’t silently change them or delay required pay.

Week 2: tighten and repeat
Hold a 15-minute manager review on Monday. Fix the biggest recurring confusion, repeat the process, and review results after Friday approval.

Measure just two things
• Swap clarity: percentage of changed shifts with replacement acceptance and manager approval before the shift starts.
• Approval timeliness: percentage of staff hours reviewed by Friday’s cutoff.

Record counts in your existing records; compare week 1 with week 2.
